title: Coptic and Ge'ez Catholics
hookLine: Egypt, Ethiopia and Eritrea have their own Catholic churches

lines: HOW CAN I, UNLESS SOMEONE SHOWS ME?
cards: An official from Ethiopia is riding home in a chariot, reading the prophet Isaiah aloud, and he can't make sense of it. A stranger runs alongside and asks whether he understands what he's reading.
How can I, the man says, unless someone shows me? That stranger is Philip, and the story is in the Acts of the Apostles.
By the end of the chapter, the man has asked to be baptized at water beside the road, and he goes on his way rejoicing. Africa is already in the story, in the New Testament itself.

teach.b: Egypt comes first. Matthew's Gospel says an angel told Joseph, in the Douay-Rheims, "Arise, and take the child and his mother, and fly into Egypt." So the Holy Family were refugees in Egypt.
Egyptian Christians, called Copts, treasure that, and tradition says the evangelist Mark later brought the Gospel to Alexandria.

Beside the Coptic Orthodox Church stands a smaller community, the Coptic Catholic Church, which prays in the same Coptic tradition, using Coptic and Arabic, in communion with Rome. Then Ethiopia and Eritrea.
Acts calls the man in the chariot "a man of Ethiopia, an eunuch," a royal treasurer. Ethiopian Christians honor him, and their own tradition tells of the faith arriving at the royal court long ago.

teach.h: GE'EZ: THE PRAYER LANGUAGE OF ETHIOPIA.
teach.b: Their ancient church language is Ge'ez, with its own script, still used in prayer though no longer spoken at home.

teach.h: SHARING NEARLY EVERYTHING WITH THE ORTHODOX.
teach.b: Here too there is an ancient Orthodox church, and alongside it two Catholic churches, the Ethiopian Catholic Church and the Eritrean Catholic Church, both praying in the Ge'ez tradition. Drums and sistrums in the liturgy.
Long fasts. White shawls. Priests carrying hand crosses that people kiss for a blessing.

teach.h: A MAN OF ETHIOPIA, AN EUNUCH.
teach.b: Last, those Orthodox neighbors. These Catholic churches share a great deal with them: the language, the music, the saints, the fasts. What differs is communion with the bishop of Rome.
The Catholic Church speaks of these Orthodox churches with deep respect, and prays for full unity, not for one to swallow the other.

how: Coptic Catholics celebrate the liturgy in the Alexandrian tradition in Coptic and Arabic; Ethiopian and Eritrean Catholics celebrate it in the Ge'ez tradition, with Ge'ez and local languages, sharing music, fasts and feasts with their Orthodox neighbors.

games.q: what does “coptic and ge'ez catholics” mean?
o: Africa's Eastern Catholics, in communion with Rome
Catholics in Africa who use only the Latin Mass
Africa's Orthodox churches, apart from Rome

games.q: Coptic and Ge'ez Catholics — tap the pairs.
p: the ancient prayer language of Ethiopia

s: Christianity reached Africa only with modern missions
Acts tells of an Ethiopian official baptized by Philip, and Matthew sends the Holy Family into Egypt.
Ge'ez is still used in prayer though it isn't spoken at home
it's the liturgical language of the Ethiopian and Eritrean churches.
the Coptic Catholic Church uses a Latin liturgy
it prays in the Coptic tradition, in Coptic and Arabic.

games.q: you're the Ethiopian official. a stranger asks if you understand the prophet you're reading. what do you say?
o: "how can I, unless someone shows me?"
games.why: he admits he needs a guide and invites Philip up into the chariot. by the end of the chapter he is baptized and goes on his way rejoicing.

practice: Picture the Horn of Africa: highlands and dry plains, a church cut into rock, a market at noon, a family on the move because of drought or war.
Then picture the man in the chariot, reading and puzzled, and the stranger who ran to help him.
If you pray, pray for Ethiopia, Eritrea and their neighbors, and for Egypt too; if you don't, hold the people of that region in your attention, with respect.

wordCard.voice: Coptic and Ge'ez Catholics. The Eastern Catholic churches of Egypt, Ethiopia and Eritrea, sharing the ancient traditions of their Orthodox neighbors and in communion with Rome. Today's word.

carryVoice: Your line: africa's ancient churches. How can I, the man asked, unless someone shows me? Rest well.
